title: Whole-mount immunofluorescent labeling of the adult fly retina
protocol: Incapacitate flies using CO2.
Place incapacitated flies in a drop of 2% PBST until anesthetized.
Transfer anesthetized flies to 1× PBS.
Attach double-sided tape on a Sylgard dissection plate.
Move each fly onto the tape by its wings using tweezers.
Cut between the head and thorax with a scalpel.
Make a small incision at either the posterior or anterior end of the head.
Place individual heads into a droplet of 4% PFA for 10-12 minutes at room temperature.
Remove fixed heads from 4% PFA and place in a droplet of 1× PBS.
Work with 3–4 heads (6–8 eyes) at a time for minimal quantification.
Transfer one head from 1× PBS onto the tape.
Cut the head along the previous incision, separating both eye tissues.
Place one eye back in 1× PBS.
Remove unwanted tissues on the other eye using a tungsten needle.
Flick the cornea off the eye tissue using the tungsten needle.
Gently place the removed cornea next to the eye tissue.
Use a pipette to transfer the finished eye into 1× PBS for later use.
Dissect one head at a time and place all heads in 1× PBS to prevent drying.
Use a dropper to place 3 drops of 0.3% PBST adjacently on a Sylgard dissection plate.
Transfer the eyes to the first drop using a pipette and slightly pipette them in the drop.
Transfer the eyes to the next drop after 10 min and repeat.
Place the desired antibodies and eyes into each individual well on the Terasaki plate.
Shake the Terasaki plate containing the eyes and antibodies for 6–12 h at 4°C.
Take out the eyes from the wells and wash them again in 0.3% PBST at 23°C-25°C, 3 times for 10 min each.
Place the desired antibodies and eyes into each individual well on the Terasaki plate.
Shake the Terasaki plate containing the eyes and antibodies for 2 h at room temperature at 25 rpm.
Remove the eyes from the Terasaki plate after 2 hours and wash them in 0.3% PBST at 23°C-25°C, 3 times for 10 min each.
Mount the eyes in mounting medium on a dissection plate using a pipette.
Transfer both the eyes and the mounting medium onto the edge of a microscopic slide with a pipette.
Use a tungsten needle to flip the compound eye upward (the curve of the eye facing up).
Place a small piece of randomly shattered cover glass near the eyes using tweezers.
With a tungsten needle, carefully place the cover glass on top of the shattered glass and eyes.
Place the cover glass at an angle to prevent direct pressure on fly eyes.
Use a pipette to fill up the remaining space between the microscopic slide and cover glass with mounting medium.
Avoid air bubbles during filling.
Cover the four corners of the cover glass with nail polish.
Let the nail polish dry completely.
